clue.text: Dear me! it's set back all the players!

parts.note: tut is the exclamation of mild disapproval, like 'dear me'

indicators.note: set back asks for the little word it to be written backwards

parts.note: it, the 's standing for 'is' and joining it to the indicator

explanation.surface: An exasperated conductor groans that the whole orchestra has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' reads as part of the exclamation, but 'set back' turns just the little word round; 'all the players' is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term marks a passage played by the whole orchestra together, every performer at once.

clue.text: Check to ensure air fares won't come down too fast

definitions.text: Check to ensure air fares won't come down too fast

parts.words: Check to ensure air fares won't come down too fast
parts.note: 'air fares' reads like ticket prices that must not drop, but it means how a new aircraft fares in the air: a trial run to be sure it will not plummet

explanation.surface: Someone wants to keep airline ticket prices from falling too sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run of a new aircraft is the check that it performs safely in the air.

clue.text: It sounds like an Asian connection

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for the Asian is to be heard, not written

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand in Asia

explanation.surface: A remark that some word resembles a link to Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A link or bond between two things is a synonym.

clue.text: Prisoner possibly on good terms with officer

parts.note: to be in with someone is to be on good terms with them
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A convict who may be friendly with a prison guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in a jail is an example of a resident of an institution; 'possibly' marks the example.

clue.text: Stoneworker pursued victim to island

parts.note: quarry is the animal or person being hunted
Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A mason chased his prey all the way to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who cuts rock from a pit is a stone labourer.

clue.text: Contractor's estimate given in marks?

definitions.meaning: a builder's priced offer for a job
words reproduced between inverted commas, i.e. a passage cited

explanation.definitionFit: A builder's price offer and a cited passage set in inverted commas share this one word.

clue.text: American investigator tailing extreme characters

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so the investigator comes after the other piece

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A US private eye shadowing some outlandish people.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient people of Mexico were native to the Americas, so one of them is an American.

clue.text: Transport going round City for duration of rally

indicators.note: going round means the transport piece encloses what follows

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a means of transport
EC is the postcode of the City of London
over can mean throughout, as in 'over the weekend'

explanation.surface: A vehicle tours the city throughout a motor rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' and 'rally' suggest a car event; RY (railway) is the transport and 'rally' is the definition, a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to bounce back, so a revival in health or prices is a synonym.

clue.text: Souvenirs from Rome and Bali I am shattering

indicators.note: shattering breaks the words into pieces to be reassembled

explanation.surface: A tourist breaks the keepsakes collected in Rome and Bali.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectable keepsakes from events or places are mementos.

clue.text: Limited number working when .PM starts

parts.note: No. is the cut-down abbreviation of number
on means functioning, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Only a few staff are in when the Prime Minister begins.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is not the Prime Minister but post meridiem, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is the moment the afternoon hours begin.

clue.text: Vessel requiring a mast to be at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship needs a mast to be out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by steam is a type of ship.

clue.text: Italian city accommodating British jazz group

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the city's letters hold the other piece

parts.note: Como is a city on Lake Como in northern Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian town plays host to a band from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small band of musicians, especially in jazz, is called this.

clue.text: Post Office issue demanding instant insurance

parts.note: read as from the very first day, at once
cover is protection under an insurance policy

explanation.surface: The Post Office puts out something requiring immediate insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanding' is a link; the surface suggests an urgent policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope with new stamps postmarked on their release date is a philatelic product of the postal service.

clue.text: Suggestive of modern accommodation for small cars

indicators.note: accommodation for means the first word houses the other

parts.note: recent means of the present era, modern
Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: Something reminds one of new garaging for compact cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Being evocative or calling something to mind is the sense shared.

clue.text: Shut English out of Irish town's sporting contest

parts.note: pent means shut up, confined

indicators.note: out of means a letter is dropped from the town's name

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the Irish Midlands

explanation.surface: An Irish town shuts the English out of its sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes the E from ATHLONE, giving ATHLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-event athletic competition is a sporting contest.

clue.text: Single doctor nursing a foot

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the pieces surround the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: An unmarried GP looks after an injured foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the metrical unit in poetry, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse a unit of an unstressed then a stressed syllable is one metrical foot.

clue.text: Spin brief tale about liaisons initially apt to be strained

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumble goes round the initial
to spin a story is to twist it, so these letters are rearranged
initially means take only the opening letter of liaisons

explanation.surface: Tell a short story about love affairs, which is liable to be sieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' makes FITERABLE, then 'about' wraps it round the initial of liaisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to be passed through a sieve or filter can be strained.

clue.text: Note about cathedral city duke's finally abandoned thus

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes round the city

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: finally abandoned drops the letter at the end of the city's name

parts.note: Hereford is an English cathedral city
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A message about a city whose duke eventually left it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally abandoned' drops the city's last letter, which is D for duke, giving HEREFOR; 'about' sets it between the two letters of the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean consequently, for that reason.

clue.text: At liberty, before autumn, to make uncontrolled descent

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: free means at liberty
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Released before the season turns, someone plummets.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop through the air unchecked, as a skydiver does before opening the chute, is this.

clue.text: Obstacles husband runs into during social events

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the social events

parts.note: dances are social events
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A married man keeps bumping into barriers at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs into' looks like a phrase, but 'into' puts R inside DANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Impediments or barriers that get in the way are obstacles.

clue.text: Conspiracy thought up by writer

explanation.definitionFit: A secret scheme and a novelist's storyline share the word.

clue.text: Inadequate container in filthy dwelling

indicators.note: in means the container piece sits inside the dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, any filthy home
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A tin left inside a squalid home is poor stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely enough or meagre is the shared sense.

clue.text: He makes rapid progress as a drug dealer

definitions.meaning: someone who goes very fast, as a racer
read literally, a trader in amphetamine, which is slang 'speed'

explanation.definitionFit: A fast mover, and literally a merchant of amphetamine, share the phrase.

clue.text: Follow scholar's teachings

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
MA is Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: A student is told to adhere to an academic's doctrines.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine laid down by authority is a body of teaching.

clue.text: Writer possibly destined for the chop?

definitions.meaning: a young sheep raised for meat, whose cutlet is a chop

explanation.definitionFit: The essayist Charles Lamb, and a young sheep that may end as cutlets, share the name.

clue.text: Sent back a time and a place for contests

indicators.note: sent back means the pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone returned a period and a venue for competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns ANERA round as a whole; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or ring where competitions are held is a venue for sport.

clue.text: Weed found in enclosed land by English lake

parts.note: grounds are the enclosed land round a building

explanation.surface: A weed growing in an estate near an English lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A common yellow-flowered wild plant is regarded as a weed.

clue.text: Main witness's pronouncement

indicators.note: pronouncement means the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: to witness is to see

explanation.surface: The chief statement from a person who saw a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old poetic word for the ocean.

clue.text: Formidable woman? One flourished in the war once

definitions.text: One flourished in the war once
definitions.meaning: an old weapon brandished in combat

explanation.definitionFit: An overbearing woman and an ancient weapon swung in combat share this name.

clue.text: Long explanation originally required in rambling story

indicators.note: required in means the initial is needed inside the story

parts.note: a yarn is a long, rambling tale

indicators.note: originally means take only the first letter of explanation

explanation.surface: A lengthy rambling tale needs an explanation at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to ache or pine for it.
